$comment: The docs#156 AC1 inventory — the closure set the meta-commentary sweep and gate rollout are measured against. 'Published surface' = a page a non-contributor is expected to read: a public repo's root README.md / CHANGELOG.md, any docs/ tree, copy staged for an external listing (.wordpress-org/, .drupalorg/), and (docs#160) published HTML reference pages. Contributor-, maintainer-, and engineering-internal documentation is exempt by design; every exemption is RECORDED here per surface with a rationale, never implied. class values: 'published' (in scope; a caller of the reusable meta-commentary-gate should cover it), 'exempt-engineering-internal' (recorded exemption), 'staged-listing' (copy staged for an external directory listing; the docs#156 AC5 ruling makes it a PUBLISHED surface — asset-production notes are removed, not exempted, and its repo's caller scans the path). An optional 'coverage' field records that something OTHER than a pinned caller enforces the gate on that surface ('repo-local' = the repo runs its own blocking check); scripts/meta-commentary-surface-coverage.mjs (docs#160 AC11) reads it and treats an ABSENT coverage as 'a caller is required' — the escape is recorded, never inferred. Recorded from each PUBLIC, non-archived org repo's default branch as of recordedAt (enumerated via the GitHub API). Archived public repos are excluded (read-only; no callers can be added) and listed in excludedArchivedRepos. Private repos publish nothing and are out of scope by definition. Regenerate by running scripts/meta-commentary-surface-coverage.mjs --live and recording what it reports; update recordedAt when doing so.
